title: Sydney Train Driver Salary 2026: Hourly to Annual Pay Guide
description: Convert a Sydney train driver salary from hourly to annual using 38-hour weeks. See base rates, tax, super, and take-home pay for Sydney Trains and Metro Melbourne.
salarySummary: A qualified Sydney Trains driver earns about $101,899 per year based on 38 hours per week, before shift penalties and overtime.

faqs.q: What is the base hourly rate for a qualified Sydney Trains driver in 2026?
faqs.a: From 1 July 2026, a qualified Sydney Trains driver (classification 'Driver Thereafter') earns $48.98 per hour, or $1,959.60 per week including the industry allowance. This is the base rate under the Sydney Trains and NSW TrainLink Enterprise Agreement 2025, approved by the Fair Work Commission. Actual take-home pay is higher due to shift penalties, weekend rates, and overtime.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect a Sydney train driver salary?
faqs.a: Casual employees in the Sydney Trains enterprise agreement receive a 25% loading on the ordinary hourly base rate instead of annual leave, sick leave, and public holidays. For a qualified driver, the casual rate would be $61.23 per hour ($48.98 × 1.25). However, most train driver roles are permanent full-time, not casual. The National Minimum Wage casual rate from 1 July 2026 is $33.05 per hour.

faqs.q: How much tax and Medicare levy does a Sydney train driver pay on $101,899?
faqs.a: Using the 2026–27 resident tax scale and the 2% Medicare levy, a Sydney train driver earning $101,899 per year would pay approximately $23,938 in tax and $2,038 in Medicare levy, leaving about $75,923 after tax (or $2,920 per fortnight). This estimate assumes no HELP repayments or Medicare levy surcharge. Superannuation of 12% is paid on top of the base salary.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Sydney Train Driver Salary

If you're looking at a **Sydney train driver salary**, you're probably comparing hourly rates, annual figures, and what you'll actually take home after tax and super. This guide uses the latest enterprise agreement rates to show you how to convert an hourly rate to annual pay, what the base salary is, and how tax and super affect your pocket.

Train drivers in Sydney are covered by the *Sydney Trains and NSW TrainLink Enterprise Agreement 2025*, approved by the Fair Work Commission. The rates in this article are from that agreement and from the summary, which tracks the official pay schedules. We'll focus on the qualified driver rate (classification 'Driver Thereafter') from 1 July 2026.

## How to Convert Hourly to Annual Salary

The standard formula for annual salary is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For full-time employees, the ordinary hours are 38 per week (76 per fortnight). This is the standard assumption used by the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Australian Bureau of Statistics. So if you have an hourly rate, multiply it by 38, then by 52 to get the annual figure.

For example, a qualified Sydney Trains driver earns $48.98 per hour (base rate excluding industry allowance). That gives:

$48.98 × 38 × 52 = $96,784 per year

But the enterprise agreement also includes a weekly industry allowance. When that's added, the weekly rate becomes $1,959.60, which works out to $101,899 per year. That's the figure you'll see in most salary discussions.

**Fortnightly pay** is simply the weekly rate multiplied by two. For a qualified driver, that's $3,919.20 before tax, or about $3,030 after tax (using the 2026–27 tax rates and Medicare levy).

## Sydney Train Driver Salary Base Rates (2026)

Here are the key base rates from the enterprise agreement for Sydney Trains drivers, effective 1 July 2026. These are the rates before shift penalties, overtime, or allowances. Actual earnings are typically higher because train crew work rotating rosters that attract penalty rates.

| Classification | Hourly | Weekly (incl. allowance) | Annual |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Driver 1st Year Trainee | $44.71 | $1,797.30 | $93,460 |
| Driver 1st Year Competent | $45.65 | $1,833.05 | $95,319 |
| Driver 2nd Year | $47.86 | $1,916.95 | $99,681 |
| **Driver Thereafter** | **$48.98** | **$1,959.60** | **$101,899** |
| Driver Trainer | $54.79 | $2,180.45 | $113,383 |
| Principal Driver | $56.76 | $2,255.30 | $117,276 |

These rates come from the Sydney Trains and NSW TrainLink Enterprise Agreement 2025 and the breakdown. The agreement was approved by the Fair Work Commission and covers Sydney Trains and NSW TrainLink.

For comparison, Metro Trains Melbourne drivers earn higher base rates: a qualified driver (SPOT) gets $68.65 per hour, or $135,657 per year, according to.

## Tax, Medicare Levy, and Take-Home Pay

Once you have the annual salary, you can estimate your take-home pay using the 2026–27 resident tax rates and the Medicare levy.

**Tax rates for 2026–27:**
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

**Medicare levy:** Generally 2% of taxable income, with reductions for low-income earners.

For a Sydney train driver earning $101,899:
- Tax: approximately $23,938
- Medicare levy: approximately $2,038
- After-tax income: about $75,923 per year, or $2,920 per fortnight

This estimate assumes the full tax-free threshold, no HELP repayments, and no Medicare levy surcharge. It also assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime or salary sacrifice. You can use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page to calculate your own figures.

## Superannuation: Paid on Top

Super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your base salary. For a $101,899 salary, that's an extra $12,228 per year contributed to your super fund. The maximum contribution base for 2026–27 is $270,830, so this driver is well within the limit.

Super is not deducted from your pay; it's an additional benefit. You can learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) on our site.

## Distinguishing Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Enterprise Agreements

It's important to understand the difference between the National Minimum Wage, award rates, and enterprise agreement rates.

- **National Minimum Wage** (from 1 July 2026): $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees get a 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. This is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or agreement.
- **Award rates**: The *Rail Industry Award* covers some rail workers, but most major operators have enterprise agreements that override the award with higher rates.
- **Enterprise agreement rates**: These are negotiated between the employer and employees (or unions) and approved by the Fair Work Commission. Sydney Trains drivers are covered by such an agreement, which pays significantly more than the minimum wage.

If you're a casual employee under the enterprise agreement, you receive a 25% loading on the base hourly rate instead of paid leave. For a qualified driver, that would be $61.23 per hour. However, most train driver roles are permanent full-time.

## Using the Hourly to Annual Conversion

Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and see the annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures. If you're a casual, tick the box to add 25% loading. The tool uses the standard 38-hour week and the 2026–27 tax rates.

For example, if you're offered a Sydney train driver role at $48.98 per hour, the tool will show:
- Annual: $96,784 (base) or $101,899 (with industry allowance)
- Fortnightly: $3,723 (base) or $3,919 (with allowance)
- After-tax fortnightly: approximately $2,858 (base) or $3,030 (with allowance)

Remember that these are estimates. Your actual pay will include shift penalties, overtime, and possibly allowances, which can increase your take-home pay by 20–30%.

## Conclusion

A **Sydney train driver salary** in 2026 starts at about $101,899 per year for a qualified driver, based on 38 hours per week. This is the base rate under the enterprise agreement; actual earnings are higher due to penalty rates and overtime. When converting hourly to annual, use the formula hourly × 38 × 52. Tax and Medicare levy will reduce your gross pay, but super of 12% is paid on top. For more detailed calculations, see our [reference tables](/data) and [pay guides](/blog).
